sections.title: The Symposium
sections.content:
The Second Symposium on Problems in the Optimization of Data Communication Systems was scheduled for Stanford University on October 20-22, 1971. ACM SIGCOMM and an IEEE committee were sponsoring the event, which would include papers, panels and workshop sessions.

Vint Cerf encouraged Network Working Group participants to submit work on network protocols and file transmission. He noted that some existing RFC drafts were suitable for publication.
sections.plainLanguage: The symposium was planned as a meeting for people working on data communication systems. Network researchers were invited to share their work on protocols and file transfer.

sections.title: Topics and Submission Rules
sections.content:
The call sought papers about advances in data communication networks, communications technology, applications, communications software, system modeling and optimization, and interface problems and standards.

Full drafts could not exceed 5,000 words and had to include an informative abstract. Papers were due by June 15, 1971. The organizers expected to notify authors by July 21 and required camera-ready text and figures by August 21.
sections.plainLanguage: Authors could submit work on six broad areas, including network software and standards. Each paper needed an abstract and had a 5,000-word limit.

sections.title: Contacts and Dates
sections.content: The symposium was scheduled for October 20-22 at Stanford University. Submissions were to be mailed to V. Cerf at UCLA. P. E. Jackson at Bell Telephone Laboratories was listed as the contact for general information.
sections.plainLanguage: Authors were asked to send papers to Vint Cerf at UCLA by June 15. The meeting itself was planned for October at Stanford.
